=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2509-2540 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Recovery trusts a syntactically valid marker wherever it appears in a pipeline-authored comment, allowing attacker-influenced quoted text to redirect reports to the marker’s issue and repository.
  WHY: The highest severity is critical (Gemini); GLM assessed the risk as a NIT and not attacker-reachable because markers are normally derived from created issues, while the other reviewers found that untrusted content can be quoted in pipeline-authored comments.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2509-2540 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Recovery treats an issue whose scope marker was removed after creation as originally markerless because it verifies scope with `last_edited_at=None`.
  WHY: A matching authenticated report can then create a replacement and close the edited issue; severity is highest at high (MAJOR), while GLM and Sonnet assess the impact as bounded or reject the concern.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1014-1028; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1645-1676 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: If posting the recovery marker fails but closing the original succeeds, a later report can recover the markerless closed original again and create another replacement.
  WHY: The original has no recovery pointer, so the next recovery pass can classify it as eligible and repeat the replacement flow.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1014-1028 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When closing the original fails in the redirect branch, the code logs the failure but sends no Telegram warning.
  WHY: The original remains open and continues to match reports without the operator warning sent by the finalize path.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:992-1009 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The paginated comments read and `/user` read occur before local scope-status and author checks that can reject the recovery.
  WHY: Duplicate reports that fail those local checks still incur network reads whose results are discarded.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:992-1009 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `/user` API read occurs before the paginated comments read, so a failed comments fetch wastes the `/user` request.
  WHY: Recovery exits when comments are unavailable, but the earlier identity read has already consumed API quota.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1017-1025 | severity=low
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The redirect branch trusts the replacement marker without independently checking that the target issue is open, pipeline-authored, and heal-labeled.
  WHY: A redirect can therefore record an occurrence on an externally closed or otherwise unverified replacement; GLM characterized the attacker-reachability concern as not exploitable under normal operation.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1023-1024 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `recovery_close="done"` is initialized before the close attempt and only changed on failure, making the pre-attempt value misleading.
  WHY: The variable can appear to represent a completed close before the command runs; GLM disagreed that this init-then-override pattern is a defect.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1645-1676 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If the replacement URL does not end in `/issues/<number>`, the marker cannot be rendered, but the original may still be closed.
  WHY: A closed original without a recovery marker cannot redirect later reports to the replacement.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:6923-6933 | severity=low
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When both recovery-marker posting and closing fail, a later duplicate can be recorded on the original instead of the replacement.
  WHY: The second budget pass guards against another replacement, but the occurrence may still be attached to the original.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  EVIDENCE: Unit coverage checks cross-repo marker status, but the end-to-end redirect test uses `SELF_REPO`; no integration test exercises a recovery marker pointing to an issue in another repository.

  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: No test covers the redirect target having been externally closed before the redirect runs.

  expected_change_site: tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py, recovery test block
  confidence=[]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The forged recovery-marker-on-original-body case is not covered; the body recovery-marker scan is comment-only.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: redirect branch of `_heal_scope_recovery_evaluate` (the `gh_retry gh issue close ... || recovery_close="failed"` line) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the retried close fails, only `close=failed` appears in the log and no warning is sent.
  WHY: The original remains open and later reports continue through the redirect path, leaving the Telegram DEBUG message as the only trace.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: `_heal_scope_recovery_evaluate`, the `/user` read and the `gh api --paginate .../comments` call before `heal-scope-recovery check` | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both network reads run before local checks that can determine scope status and author trust from `${ISSUES_FILE}`.
  WHY: With recovery enabled, duplicate reports for verified-marker issues or foreign authors fetch comments whose results are discarded.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: "Test missing or forged scope, duplicate handling, and guard-off behavior."
Expected change site: tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py
Evidence of absence: There is no integration test where a recovery marker on the original points at another repository (`replaced_repo`), and none where the replacement is closed when the redirect runs; the unit test `test_heal_scope_recovery_check_statuses` covers the cross-repo marker only at the function level.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: heal_scope_recovery_check (line 2512) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A recovery marker is trusted wherever it appears in a pipeline-authored comment, including raw diagnosis comments containing attacker-influenced text.
  WHY: An attacker who can influence diagnosis comments could quote a marker pointing to an issue and repository under their control, redirecting future reports and closing the original issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: heal_scope_recovery_check (line 2512) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Recovery cannot distinguish an originally markerless issue from a pipeline-authored issue whose scope marker was later removed.
  WHY: A user who can edit the issue can remove its scope marker while leaving its fingerprint marker, allowing a verified report to recover and close the edited issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: _heal_scope_recovery_evaluate (line 992-996, 1001) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `/user` API read happens before the paginated comments fetch.
  WHY: If the comments fetch fails, the `/user` call has already consumed API quota.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: _heal_scope_recovery_evaluate (line 1023-1024) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `recovery_close="done"` is set before the `gh issue close` attempt.
  WHY: If the close fails, the value is misleading.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: _heal_scope_recovery_evaluate (line 1014-1028) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If finalize posts a recovery marker unsuccessfully but closes the original issue successfully, no marker prevents a later report from recovering the already-closed original again.
  WHY: Closed issues remain in budget/duplicate matching, so repeated reports can create additional replacements when marker posting fails and closing succeeds.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: _heal_scope_recovery_evaluate (line 1014-1028) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If closing the original issue fails in the redirect branch, no Telegram warning signals that the original remains open.
  WHY: The original issue can remain open without an operator signal, unlike the main finalize path.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: Test missing or forged scope, duplicate handling, and guard-off behavior.
Expected change site: tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py recovery test block
Evidence of absence: The recovery test suite does not cover (a) a forged `ai:workflow-heal-scope:v1` marker placed directly on the original issue body by the trusted author; (b) cross-repo redirect when the recovery marker points to an issue in a different repository; or (c) the case where the redirected replacement has been externally closed before the redirect runs.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
